name: east

attributes.attribute: the direction of commerce and wealth in old Irish thought
the direction of sunrise, beginnings and openings
the province located in the east, tied to youthful vigor

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: In the old Irish scheme of directions, east ruled commerce and wealth. It stood opposite the western province of wisdom. Because the sun rises there, east meant beginnings and openings. East also holds the province of Leinster. That land carries youthful vigor and enterprise. The entry sends the reader to the directions entry for the full scheme.

okr.objective: Define east as a directional concept of commerce, wealth and fresh beginnings.
key_results: East was the Irish direction of commerce and wealth.
It stood opposite the western province of wisdom.
East meant beginnings and openings as the direction of sunrise.
The province of Leinster sits in the east and signals youthful vigor.
